newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB takes 3-yr credit from Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB takes 3-yr credit from Dresdner.

text.p: The Czech bank Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. said on Thursday that it had signed an agreement for a $20 million three-year loan for export credits from Dresdner Bank priced at 25 basis points above LIBOR.
"The three-year loan is to be drawn in American dollars and in German marks. It is intended for pre-export and export financing of IPB clients," IPB spokesman Jan Rezek said in a statement.
The rate for the credit was not nearly as affordable as recent international credits granted to the Czech National Bank (CNB) and the state-run Czech Export Bank.

By comparison, the CNB earlier this month closed a $1.5 billion syndicated one-year revolving credit line at 10 basis points above Libor with reportedly another 2.5 basis points added if more than fifty percent of the facility is drawn.
The CNB late last week raised the total volume of the credit line, to be used as a safety net for foreign currency reserves, to $2 billion.
A recent Eurobond for the Czech Export Bank was priced at 12.5 basis points above Libor.
